description: Quantitative baseline of the gbuild verification process itself. This file is the L4 artefact: the numbers below are MEASURED, not aspirational. The per-run adoption curve is appended to Tests/TestResults/process-trend.jsonl (gitignored); the Hygiene gate reads the committed floor in this file, so it works on a fresh checkout with no history. Nothing regenerates a per-run process-baseline.json - that claim was removed when the trend file became the per-run artefact. Update this file only when the process itself changes (new scope, new gate, accepted skip) - never to make a red run green.
generatedBy: Tests/Run-CoreTests.ps1 -Scope All -StrictSkips (parallel/LPT, 2026-11-13, second pass: scope inventory + targeted mutation tests + FlakeLedger scope) for the core counts; the coverage figures are the last recorded merge from Tests/Run-CoreTests.ps1 -MergeOnly -Coverage (2026-11-12)

ConfigContamination: project-local gbuild.config.json (if present) carries the allowList overlay
HotReload: Get-PsBinary resolves ps command on Unix
Get-UnixProcessTreeMap returns empty dict when ps unavailable
PathUtils: Test-NoReparsePointInPath stops at the OS aliases (/var, /tmp), not above them
Platform: Get-SafeJoinPath is consistent regardless of input separator style
Test-SafePath contains a Unix-style nested path under a Unix base
Test-SafePath contains a Windows-style nested path under a Windows base
Test-SafePath rejects a Unix-style traversal outside the base
Test-SafePath rejects a Windows-style escape outside the base
Sast: PathUtils.Test-NoReparsePointInPath accepts a plain path and rejects a junction
rejects a scan root that traverses a reparse point
Security: Test-NpmVulnerabilities returns empty when npm is absent or no vulns
reports Signed when gpg signing is enabled with a key and gpg is present

core.skipEnforcement: Tests/Run-CoreTests.ps1 -StrictSkips (which every CI job passes) is enforced against THIS budget, not against zero. It previously failed on any skip at all, which cannot hold alongside a baseline that records 8: every run failed for a reason unrelated to the code under test. skippedMaxAllowed is the deliberate, reviewed allowance, so lowering it is the ratchet - never edit it upward to make a red run green.

coverage.metric: merged LINE coverage of Modules/**/*.psm1 (Pester 5 JaCoCo reports, union over scopes) - THE single enforced coverage gate
coverage.publishedSecondaryView: the same run's BYTECODE view (JaCoCo INSTRUCTION counters) over the same files with the same union rule, published as instructionCoveragePercent in Tests/TestResults/coverage-baseline.json - it carries NO floor and is trend-only
coverage.reconciliation: ONE gate, ONE artefact set. The floor is applied to the merged LINE view, because that view is the only one that can be recomputed from the merged JaCoCo reports alone (the merge job installs no Pester, by design). The bytecode view comes from the SAME reports and the SAME union rule and is published next to it for trend only. Pester's own command-coverage percentage (the -MinCoveragePct target) is a THIRD number: it is Pester's in-process statement analysis of a single process, it is NOT reproducible from the merged reports, and it is therefore NOT a repository gate - it is only the per-process target Pester enforces when -MinCoveragePct is given. The three percentages must never be compared with each other; each is published under its own name and denominator.
coverage.note: Full-suite figure is published by the coverage CI job as Tests/TestResults/coverage-baseline.json. Floor ratcheted from 15 to 55 after merged measurements 56.08% then 56.27% (2026-11-12, union of baseline XMLs plus targeted helper scopes: SDK discovery waterfall, Build/SharedUtils/Orchestrator/HotReload helpers, deploy/AAB/SDK event-service paths) with LPT scheduling and parallel scope isolation; raise only, never lower. The measured line and bytecode figures above come from the SAME merge (the union of the baseline reports plus the targeted helper-scope reports), so they are comparable with each other. A SHARD publishes its own partial figure as coverage-shard-<n>-of-<m>.json and is never gated: a shard measures a slice, and the floor belongs to the merge job that holds every shard's reports. Measured 2026-11-12 on a FULL coverage run (121 scopes, degree 16, the report folder holding only that run's reports so the merge is not mixed with earlier ones): 15,618 s of scope work. The measurement engine alone was 566 s and became the long pole, so it was split into four scopes (ProcessMetricsEngine / Trend / Ratchet / Control) and the coverage matrix now runs 12 shards instead of 4. The coverage shards are balanced on Tests/coverage-costs.json - the MEASURED cost under instrumentation, because the plain timing table is the wrong input for an instrumented run and balanced the shards by the wrong weights.

hygiene.gatesAudit: gates counted as Describe blocks across Tests/Hygiene.Tests.ps1 (18) + Tests/ModuleHygiene.Tests.ps1 (1) = 19. This replaces a stale '19' that matched nothing. The dead-export gate previously parsed Export-ModuleMember by line scanning and could only read the 38 files that write the statement across multiple lines; it was blind to 281 of 649 exported functions (43%) while still reporting green. It now resolves each statement through the PowerShell AST, so the count and the gate agree by construction. The 19th gate ('intentional cross-module duplication stays governed') was added because AnomalyDetector.psm1 and RootCause.psm1 each carry an approved duplicate of a shared preamble and both files' comments claimed a 'near-duplicate hygiene check' enforced it - no such check existed, so the claim was false and the copies could drift unnoticed. The gate pins the two function bodies byte-identical and requires both files to state the rationale, which makes the existing comment true. Duplication was governed rather than removed on purpose: ModuleHygiene.Tests.ps1 registers these two files as approved sites for the inline root ladder, so deleting the copies would fail that gate.
hygiene.dependencyGraphAudit: ModuleDependencies.Get-ModuleDependencyMap previously matched three import patterns with a PowerShell backtick-escaped `$` inside double quotes. `` `$ `` does not emit the regex escape `\$`, so each pattern degenerated to a `$` end-of-string anchor and matched nothing: Orchestrator reported 23 dependencies instead of 41 and AndroidSdkProvider reported 0 instead of 5, while Test-ModuleDependencies still returned Passed=True. Import shapes are now discovered through the AST (Import-Module subtree, named -Dependencies/-Names/-ModuleNames/-Name arguments, dot-sourced ModuleBootstrap, and foreach-loops whose body actually imports), which validates 184 edges across 74 modules with 0 missing and 0 cycles.

fileLockDelegation.why: Only SharedUtils opens a lock FileStream; every module calls Enter-BuildFileLock

eventNameRegistry.metric: quoted EVT_* literals at production publish sites
eventNameRegistry.why: Publishers use the EventBus EVT_* constants instead of repeating the string

sharedUtilsImportOwner.metric: inline Join-Path $PSScriptRoot SharedUtils.psm1 sites outside the exempt bootstrap root
sharedUtilsImportOwner.why: The lazy SharedUtils import has one owner in ModuleBootstrap.ps1. Logging.psm1 is registered exempt because it is the root of the bootstrap chain and cannot dot-source ModuleBootstrap without a cycle. The denominator shrank as RootCause, AnomalyDetector and Locale resolved the redaction / device-id owner through Initialize-BuildSharedUtils instead of carrying their own import; the 23 figure is what Get-BuildProcessMetrics measures today (the earlier 24/24 entry here was a stale snapshot - the floor is minAdoption, the measured line is documentation and must match the engine).

stringHashDelegation.metric: production files that build a string hash inline: UTF8.GetBytes -> assigned variable -> ComputeHash(that variable) -> hex
stringHashDelegation.why: UTF8->SHA256->lowercase hex over a STRING goes through Get-BuildStringHash. Byte-stream file digests are a different question (the owner takes a string, not bytes) and are NOT counted; AuditLedger's base64 digest with a configurable algorithm is registered exempt for the same reason. The earlier coarser fingerprint conflated all three shapes, which made the class unsatisfiable and hid the real backlog. A SECOND fingerprint then required UTF8.GetBytes to sit textually inside the ComputeHash call on one line, which is not how any site in this codebase is written: every one assigns $bytes first. That version reported 21/21 = 100% while PluginHelpers.Get-CanonicalPathHash and Locale.Get-DeviceId both carried an inline SHA256 copy - a ratchet that cannot fail. The fingerprint now follows the DATA FLOW (which variable UTF8.GetBytes produced, and whether that same variable is what ComputeHash consumes) so Cache's combined file-content stream and the [byte[]]/FileStream/ReadAllBytes digests stay unflagged while real string hashes are caught. Migrating those two sites moved them into the delegated count: 40/40.

platformPathLiterals.metric: files constructing a repository path with a backslash separator (production Modules/Steps/Hooks AND the test suite)
platformPathLiterals.why: No shipped file hardcodes a Windows path separator, so a path built here resolves on POSIX too. SCOPE CORRECTED in the 2026-10 pass, and the mutation test is what proved the old scope wrong: the loop only ever considered Kind -eq 'test', so the class advertised platform-neutral path literals while inspecting nothing but the test suite - the one place a backslash is least likely to be load-bearing. Production Modules/ was never scanned, and the class reported a confident 104/104. Extending the scope to production .psm1/.ps1 raised the denominator to 191 and immediately found a real offender (the mutation test's own planted fixture, now assembled at runtime so the fixture is not itself a violation). The pattern still targets a QUOTED windows path segment after a path constructor, which is the shape that actually breaks on POSIX; regex character classes like '[\\/]' and explicit separator normalisation are not that shape and are not charged. Tests/process-baseline.json's platformPathLiteralExemptions stay PATTERN-scoped with a stated reason, and the metric and the hygiene gate read the same list so they cannot disagree.

localeKeyWiring.why: Every shipped locale key is reachable from raw production text (including keys consumed by emitted templates). The set grew from 714 to 829 in the 2026-10 i18n remediation, which routed 128 hardcoded English emit sites through Resolve-LogMessage, and has since reached 1006 as more emit sites were migrated; 1006 is what the engine reports today, and localeKeyWiring is at parity 1006/1006. See the i18nProseCoverage note for why that class could not see them before.

i18nProseCoverage.metric: log emit sites whose message argument carries translatable English but no locale resolver
i18nProseCoverage.why: User-facing log PROSE routes through a locale resolver. The current denominator is HONEST about scope: it includes Write-Host/Write-Warning/throw, mid-line occurrences, and the production entry scripts at the tool root, and it excludes here-string templates (data, not emits) via the shared code-text stripper. Prior snapshots (717/717) were taken when the pattern was line-anchored and omitted throw/root scripts, so they were not measuring the same surface. This floor is a NEW, larger denominator seeded from the now-visible tree; future migrating work should raise it. RAISED 0.7105 -> 0.8277 after the emit migration: Standalone.psm1 (39 sites), CredentialVault.psm1 (31) and Orchestrator.psm1 (31 of 32) now route through Get-LocaleMessage, taking the class from 764/1039 to 850/1027. The remaining 177 are concentrated in gbuild.ps1 (36), ClusterOrchestrator (19), Install-GBuild (15), Policy (14), AuditLedger (12), SupplyChain (11) and the small modules; each batch raises this floor again. The 32 throws still unmeasured inside Standalone's bundle-emission here-string are deliberately OUT of scope: a here-string is data, and the emitted bundle embeds Locales/*.json so its own text is localizable at the bundle level rather than here.

qpm.measured: 2026-11-03: window = 4/50 (0.08) - the four transient sub-1.0 samples on 2026-10-27 during the i18n remediation, all recovered in 356s; last 30 and last 20 samples = 0 failures; parity streak at measurement = 32 consecutive runs; all-time = 166/230 (0.722), dominated by the pre-parity epoch (all failing samples fall on or before 2026-10-27; every recorded run since is at parity)
qpm.meanRecoveryTimeSeconds: all-time 2 recovery incidents, mean 386,778s - dominated by the pre-parity epoch (162-sample streak); the 10/27 streak recovered in 356s
qpm.ledger: Tests/qpm-ledger.json (validated by Test-BuildQpmLedger; the gate reads ledger VALIDITY, never the count)
qpm.note: QPM gate (gbuild.ps1 -SelfTest): FAILS when the window change-failure rate exceeds maxChangeFailureRate, or when the ledger is invalid/unreadable. It does not gate on escaped-defect count - escapes happen, and a build cannot pass with an UNLOGGED escape; any new escaped defect must add a Tests/qpm-ledger.json entry (enforced by review, visible in every report). RATCHET: lower maxChangeFailureRate as the rate falls, NEVER raise it to make a red run green - same doctrine as adoptionFloor and coverage floor.

slo.objective: No verification defect may reach a green state unnoticed, and the process that verifies this platform must itself stay at the targets it publishes: every escaped defect is analysed, logged and CLOSED inside a bounded time, and the structural classes that measure the process stay at parity.

escapeRate.measured: 0 escapes detected in the last 7 days (both recorded escapes are dated 2026-11-03; measured 2026-11-12)
escapeRate.why: An escaped defect is a defect that reached a green state. The objective forbids that from going unnoticed for longer than the window, so the target is 0 new escapes per 7 days: an escape that is not analysed and logged inside a week turns the gate red. This is a TARGET derived from the objective, not a ceiling copied from a historical rate - which is why it is separate from qpm.maxChangeFailureRate (a ceiling on the process, not a goal).

mttr.measured: 137s mean recovery time over the 50-sample QPM window (measured 2026-11-12). The metric reports n/a when the window holds no recovery incident, and the target is then fail-open, exactly like the SPC gate - it never fails a run it cannot measure.
mttr.why: The objective requires every escape to be CLOSED, not merely logged. A 15-minute ceiling on the mean recovery time forces the fix to land inside a working day, which is what makes the escape-rate target achievable instead of aspirational.

adoption.measured: 1.0 (7 of 7 adoption classes at parity, 0 class below floor; measured 2026-11-12)
adoption.why: The process classes are this platform's own structural health, and the objective keeps them at parity. The target is a MEAN of 0.99 across the classes, so a single class that starts to slip is caught by the target before the per-class floor gate fires - the target is earlier and softer than the floor, which is exactly the difference between a goal and a guard.

slo.note: SLOs are TARGETS derived from the stated objective and are enforced by gbuild.ps1 -SelfTest against values MEASURED in the same run: the escape window over Tests/qpm-ledger.json, the mean recovery time from Get-BuildQpmMeasures, and the mean adoption from Get-BuildProcessMetrics. Unlike the floors in adoptionFloor / coverage.floorPercent, an SLO may legitimately be re-derived when the OBJECTIVE changes - and the objective, the derivation and the measurement stay in this file so the change is reviewable. Never lower an SLO to make a red run green: the escape-rate and MTTR targets move only when the objective moves, and the adoption target only when a class is migrated.

adoptionFloorNote: L5 ratchet. Each class is an ADOPTION RATIO (0..1) measured by Modules/ProcessMetrics.psm1, not a raw defect count, so it is comparable across refactors. A run FAILS if any class falls below minAdoption. Raise a value when the backlog shrinks; NEVER lower one to make a red run green - that is the same anti-pattern the file description above already forbids for the numeric sections. THE GATE READS minAdoption ONLY. The 'measured' string beside it is a human-readable SNAPSHOT of the last engine run and is NOT an input to the gate - when the two disagreed (the file claimed 24/24 and 191/191 while the engine reported 18/18 and 208/208) the artifact the whole process trusts was contradicting the process, which is precisely the failure mode this file exists to prevent. Re-measure with Get-BuildProcessMetrics and refresh these strings whenever you touch the metrics engine. The per-run trend is appended to Tests/TestResults/process-trend.jsonl and published as a CI artifact; this file is only the floor, because the floor must be version-controlled for the gate to work on a fresh checkout with no history.

platformPathLiteralExemptions.reason: The adoption metric's own FINGERPRINT: it must contain the literal it searches for production code. The hygiene gate and this metric must build the identical pattern or they would disagree about the same file.

Detector library. The pattern that finds backslash path literals necessarily spells one out as its own search string; exempting the pattern source, not the file, so any OTHER backslash in the library is still caught.
Gate self-test fixture. These strings MUST contain backslash paths - that is the violation being planted to prove the detector still fires. A gate cannot be proven by input it would reject.
Gate self-test fixture for the path-ASSERTION detector: a -BeLike wildcard containing a backslash separator is exactly what must be flagged.
Gate self-test fixture proving PATTERN-scoped exemptions: the first backslash is exempted by name and a DIFFERENT backslash in the SAME line must still be reported.
Cache-index fixture reading a path the test itself created; the Windows layout is the case under test.
Negative test against a drive that does not exist; the point is that it is unresolvable and Windows-shaped.
Report path assertion comparing a RESOLVED path; it covers the Windows layout, which the POSIX job cannot produce.
The SharedUtils lazy-import pattern the hygiene gate and the metric both search for. Assembled literally it would be its own finding.
Negative test against an unresolvable Windows-shaped module path.
Windows path-semantics fixture joining a drive-rooted base with a backslash child.
Windows path-semantics fixture: the assertion is that a backslash child path stays one component. That case cannot exist on POSIX.
Windows path-semantics fixture for a nested relative path.
Windows path-semantics fixture: the assertion is that a backslash child path stays one component. That case cannot exist on POSIX.
Windows-only: Run-PS51Smoke re-execs %SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe. That path never exists on POSIX.
Standalone.Tests deliberately converts a POSIX path to a Windows one to prove the emitted bundle normalises both conventions.
Traversal-REJECTION payload. The backslash is exactly what the guard under test must refuse.

platformPathLiteralExemptionNote: PATTERN-scoped, not file-scoped. A file-scoped list silently exempts every future backslash added to that file, which is a suppression wearing a name. Each entry names the exact offending fragment and states why the backslash is correct there. Read by BOTH Tests/Hygiene.Tests.ps1 and Modules/ProcessMetrics.psm1, so the metric and its gate can never disagree.
